ai.description: This lizard reaches 20–25 cm. It is olive-brown with a pale throat and dark crossbands. Key features include a prominent, fan-like gular fold and a short, blunt snout. Family: Agamidae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ptyctolaemus gularis* is best distinguished by the prominent, fan-like gular fold (dewlap) that lacks the distinct scales or bright color patches found in similar agamas.
ai.habitat: *Ptyctolaemus gularis* inhabits moist, dense evergreen and subtropical broadleaf forests in the Himalayas and Northeast India, typically at altitudes between 600 and 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Green Fan-throated Lizard is primarily diurnal and employs a unique defensive strategy by extending its colorful throat fan to startle potential predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ptyctolaemus gularis* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 2–4 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between May and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ptyctolaemus gularis* is found in Northeast India (Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Mizoram) and neighboring regions, inhabiting forests at elevations of 500–2,000m.
